say.en: When something goes wrong, does anyone ever say, "It was my fault"? In Melon City, everyone points at someone else. In this lesson: Trace the chain of blame.
Explain how the architect shifts the blame to the king.
Identify what the chain of blame satirises.

body.en: Furious, the king orders the chief of builders to be hanged. The chief *blames* the workmen; the workmen blame the masons for making bricks of the wrong size; the masons blame the architect. Each group escapes by pointing at the next.

say.en: The king orders the chief builder to be hanged.
The chief builder blames the workmen.
The workmen blame the masons for wrong-sized bricks.
The masons blame the architect.
The architect says the king changed the plans.
The blame returns to the king, who is confused.

body.en: The architect reminds the king that he himself had made changes to the plans. The blame has come full circle, and the king is confused. Seth uses this circular *chain* to mock people who never accept responsibility and a system where punishment is decided before the facts.

points.en: Architect: the king amended the plans
Satire: passing the buck; hasty justice
